title: Cross-Lingual Retrieval
summary: Retrieve evidence across languages using evaluated multilingual representations or translation paths while preserving source meaning and access scope.
overview: Cross-lingual retrieval lets a query in one language find relevant documents written in another. A multilingual embedding model can place supported languages in a shared space; an alternative translates the query or documents before retrieval. These strategies differ in cost, coverage, and vulnerability to mistranslated terminology.

Language support is not binary. Quality varies by language pair, script, domain, and document style. Product names, legal terms, units, and abbreviations often require exact preservation. Retrieval, reranking, answer generation, and citation rendering must all be evaluated across the languages actually used, not inferred from an English benchmark.

production.poc: A prototype builds a bilingual evaluation set with native-reviewed relevance labels.
production.production: Production records source language, preserves original text, and uses terminology dictionaries where translation is required.
production.scale: Enterprise scale monitors low-resource language slices, model-version drift, regional permissions, and translation costs separately from generation costs.

components.name: Language detector
components.role: Identifies likely languages and mixed-language inputs without forcing uncertain classification.

components.name: Multilingual encoder
components.role: Embeds queries and documents in a compatible evaluated representation.

components.name: Translation adapter
components.role: Provides an optional controlled path with terminology and identity preservation.

components.name: Cross-lingual reranker
components.role: Orders retrieved evidence using supported language-pair evaluation.

components.name: Citation presenter
components.role: Links original sources and labels translated excerpts clearly.

flow.title: Identify language needs
flow.description: Determine query language, desired answer language, and permitted source languages.

flow.title: Preserve key terms
flow.description: Extract identifiers, numbers, and domain terms that must survive transformation.

flow.title: Choose retrieval path
flow.description: Use shared embeddings, translated queries, or a measured combination.

flow.title: Retrieve under scope
flow.description: Apply the same authorization and temporal constraints regardless of language.

flow.title: Validate relevance
flow.description: Rerank with a compatible model and verify critical terminology in original sources.

flow.title: Answer with provenance
flow.description: Respond in the requested language while retaining original citations and marking translations.

diagrams.caption: The answer language can differ from the evidence language without losing source provenance.

useCase.title: Serving technicians across regional manuals
useCase.situation: A vehicle manufacturer supports technicians who ask in Spanish while some engineering bulletins are published first in German.
useCase.problem: English-centric retrieval misses relevant bulletins or mistranslates component identifiers.
useCase.requirement: Find authoritative cross-language evidence and preserve exact part numbers and applicability.
useCase.architecture: A multilingual index combines original bulletins with a controlled terminology dictionary and language-tested reranking.
runtime: A Spanish query retains its component code while entering the multilingual retriever.
The answer cites the German bulletin and labels its translated explanation.
useCase.failure: If a critical technical term remains ambiguous, the assistant shows the source phrase and routes the interpretation for specialist review.
useCase.impact: Measure retrieval recall and terminology accuracy per language pair; a single multilingual average can conceal an unusable regional experience.

tradeoffs.cost: May perform unevenly across languages and domains.
Users may need translated excerpts to interpret them.

failures.detection: The retrieved component differs from the requested code.
failures.recovery: Protect identifiers and compare them before search.

failures.detection: Relevant cross-language candidates fall in rank.
failures.recovery: Use a validated multilingual scorer or a tested fallback.

mistakes.mistake: Assuming all languages have equal quality
mistakes.fix: Evaluate actual language pairs and domain slices.
Store originals and link translations by version.

mistakes.mistake: Dropping access filters on translated search
mistakes.fix: Carry the same trusted scope through every path.

whenToUse: Use for multilingual enterprises with shared knowledge.
Use when queries and authoritative documents differ in language.
Use when regional terminology has been evaluated.
whenNotToUse: Avoid unsupported languages without an explicit fallback.
Do not translate exact identifiers casually.
Avoid relying on machine translation alone for ambiguous critical instructions.
checklist: Label translated excerpts and retain citations.
